prompt: Appraiser Ruth completes a refinance appraisal ordered by First Harbor Bank. The homeowner, who paid the $550 appraisal fee at application, calls and asks her to email him the report and value today. What should Ruth do?

options.text: Refer him to the bank; release results only with its consent
Email him the report, since the homeowner paid the appraisal fee
Send a copy, because ECOA requires borrowers to receive one
Tell him the value by phone but hold back the written report

explanation: Under the USPAP Ethics Rule, assignment results are confidential to the client, here the bank. Ruth may disclose them only to the client, parties the client authorizes, state regulators, due process of law, or a peer review committee. Paying the fee does not make the borrower a client.

distractorExplanations.b: Who pays the fee does not decide who the client is; the bank engaged Ruth, so the homeowner needs the bank's authorization first.
distractorExplanations.c: ECOA's copy rule binds the lender, not the appraiser; the bank delivers the copy, and Ruth's duty is to protect assignment results.
distractorExplanations.d: The value conclusion is itself an assignment result, so stating it by phone breaches confidentiality just as sending the report would.

prompt: Appraiser Marcus values a 35-year-old single-family home in a subdivision with six recent, similar sales and very few rentals. He developed all three approaches. In reconciliation, which indication deserves the most weight?

options.text: An average of the three, so their errors offset
Cost approach, as replacement cost is easy to verify
Income approach, using a GRM from the few rentals
Sales comparison, backed by six recent sales

explanation: Reconciliation weighs each approach by the quality and quantity of its data and its relevance to how buyers act. Six recent similar sales make sales comparison the strongest indication; the cost approach weakens as accrued depreciation grows on a 35-year-old home, and sparse rentals undercut the income approach.

distractorExplanations.a: Reconciliation is not averaging; USPAP expects the appraiser to weigh each approach by data quality and explain the final choice.
distractorExplanations.b: Building cost is verifiable, but estimating 35 years of accrued depreciation is subjective, which makes the cost indication weak here.
distractorExplanations.c: A GRM drawn from very few rentals is thinly supported, and buyers of owner-occupied homes in this subdivision do not price them on rent.
